_doc: English words that other products' listings use in passing ('freshly prepared', 'family pack', 'golden brown', 'light meat', 'super saver'). catalog_match.brand_index.is_generic_brand(phrase) calls a brand phrase generic when every significant token of it is in 'words' (a plural 's' is folded, so 'Green Farms' counts as 'green farm'); catalog_match.score then accepts such a brand's hit as full brand evidence only where a brand stands (the start of the product part of a title, the start of the page slug's product segment) or on the brand's official domain. Tokens are catalog_match.text_norm tokens ('SUPER/T' is 'super t'). Not significant, so they neither make a phrase generic nor distinctive: single letters ('t' in 'Super T', initials) and the articles, conjunctions and honorifics under 'ignored' ('Al Fresh' is judged on 'fresh', 'Mr John' on 'john'). A digit token ('7 Up') or an Arabic token is significant and never common, and a phrase made only of ignored tokens and single letters is not generic. Curation: one lower-case token per entry; add a word only when it is common in other brands' listing text. Given names ('john') and words that would turn a well-known distinctive brand generic without a real case ('garden' of American Garden) stay out.
